Alex — thanks for the clear list. Recap below and proposed next steps. I copied Rishi (security) and Dev (support) for technical details and attachments.

Summary (short):
- PII & retention: Redwood Private supports per-tenant retention policies and can configure automatic purging. For strict PII handling we recommend tenant-level encryption with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) so we never hold plaintext keys.
- Logging & audit: We provide request/response logs and an audit log for admin actions. Immutable storage for audit logs is supported via WORM storage options in the Private offering; retention windows are configurable up to 7 years.
- Access controls / RBAC: Role-based access with customizable roles + attribute-based policies. Fine-grained scopes for model access, route access, and administrative actions.
- Support access / break-glass: Support engineers require explicit, time-bound break-glass approvals and all sessions are recorded and audited. Break-glass requires approval chain (customer SSO + on-call manager) and generates an immutable entry in the audit log.

Attachments: Rishi attached a short RBAC overview and Dev attached our SOC2 evidence checklist for your procurement team.

On Fri, May 28, 2027 at 09:22 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:

> Alex / Marissa — quick technical notes to expand on RBAC and break-glass:
> 
> RBAC model (high level):
> - Roles: viewer, operator, model-invoker, admin, compliance-auditor. Roles are tenant-scoped and support hierarchical delegation.
> - Scopes: model:invoke, model:manage, route:configure, logs:view, audit:export.
> - Attribute-based policies: tie roles to SAML/SCIM groups and optional IP / time-of-day constraints.
> 
> Least privilege templates (examples):
> - Application integration: model:invoke only, logs:view (redacted payloads), no admin or model:manage.
> - Support engineer (tier 1): logs:view (redacted), ticket:annotate, no access to raw request bodies.
> - Break-glass role: time-limited model:invoke + logs:view, must be approved via customer SSO + two Redwood on-call approvals. All break-glass activations create an immutable audit entry and trigger email to customer security.
> 
> Support access controls:
> - Support engineers cannot access raw plaintext payloads unless break-glass is activated. When activated, full session capture (screen + command audit) is stored in immutable audit logs.
> - We can require customer-signed JIT approvals through your IdP (SAML).
> 
> Implementation notes for Private deployment:
> - Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM (syslog/Kafka) and to an object store configured with WORM.
> - For zero-trust we recommend enabling tenant-level KMS and SCIM provisioning.
>
